title: Rules engine design places Drools in the recovery module, Architecture v5 places it in each service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx
section: 1 The design on one page; 6 Runtime
description: Version 3 states that rules are evaluated by Drools embedded in the recovery module, with one Spring service inside the module as the runtime. Architecture v5 slide 27 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 state that each of the 19 services carries its own embedded Drools engine and evaluates the model it owns, with the registry in rwb-decision. The two statements cannot both hold for the target.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 1: 'Rules are evaluated by Drools embedded in the recovery module'; section 6: 'The runtime is one Spring service inside the recovery module'. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27: 'RUN IN THE OWNING SERVICE (e.g. rwb-valuation)'. Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11: 'Each of the 19 Recovery services has the same shape: its own Temporal worker and queue, an embedded Drools engine, its own schema'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: Keep Architecture v5 (R-PREC item 1 and 2): embedded Drools in each service, registry in rwb-decision; version 3 wording kept as the superseded statement in sections 1 and 6.

title: Owning service of the PAYMENT_MATCH package is not stated in one place
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: The Temporal and Drools design slide 18 states that S2 already has three Drools packages in Phase 1 (RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH, BOOKING_MATCH), while Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-payment the matchPayments activity (JOB-07) that finds the missed payment and slide 41 gives rwb-treatment only treatments, contracts and agreements. The design does not say which service loads and evaluates the PAYMENT_MATCH model.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18: 'S2 already has three Drools packages in Phase 1'. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 rwb-payment IN: 'TMP Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings'; slide 41 rwb-treatment owns 'treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: S2 rwb-treatment owns and evaluates PAYMENT_MATCH, and the matchPayments activity of P8 rwb-payment asks S2 for the answer through S2's contract; recorded as an assumption until the package is authored.

title: RuleCatalog and the rule store are one interface in version 3 and two owners in the target
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Version 3 publishes RuleCatalog and RulePackageRepository as interfaces of the one runtime, reading rule_row and the version tables. The Ownership Map places rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case with P7 in schema rwb_decision. The design therefore has to say whether an owning service calls its own RuleCatalog or the registry's.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 6 component table: 'RuleCatalog | Published interface ... returns ... from rule_row only'. Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owner P7, schema rwb_decision, ruling 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: RuleCatalog, RulePackageRepository and the four rule tables are served by rwb-decision (P7); an owning service asks the registry through its contract and keeps no copy of rule_row.

title: Fact class of each package is named for the single module, not for a service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx
section: 3 The rule row and its Drools decision-table columns
description: The Import column example reads recovery.casewf.rules.facts.AllocationFacts, a class of the single recovery module. In the target each service has its own Java package, th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.<short without hyphen> (Rules R4), and the sources do not give the fact class name of any of the 448 rules.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 3 table: 'Import | recovery.casewf.rules.facts.AllocationFacts'. Template and Rules R4: Java package 'th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.<short without hyphen>'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: The Import line names the owning service's fact class; the exact class names are Not specified in the source documents and are settled when the packages are authored.

title: The model load path GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} is in the architecture and in no interface catalogue
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: 4 Version lifecycle; 6 Runtime; 10.1 What each service carries
description: Architecture v5 slides 14, 18 and 27 give a service GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} to fetch an approved model version and rwb-decision POST /rule-models to publish one. The Ownership Map Endpoints sheet lists the /admin/rule-package and /admin/rule-version paths but no /rule-models path, and the published API specification does not carry it either.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 rwb-decision IN: 'GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}'; slide 27: 'Load GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in'. Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: /admin/rule-packages and /admin/rule-versions rows only.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: rwb-decision serves the model fetch on the Architecture v5 wording under /api/recovery/decision/v1; the operation name and payload are confirmed in API Specification v5.

title: Delivery ownership of E1-072 and E1-073 differs between the story set and the Ownership Map
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (legacy); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: The split plan gives RWB-E1-072 the primary PLT and RWB-E1-073 the primary P3, with P3, P4, P6, P7 and P2 slices. Every rule-package and rule-version endpoint in the Ownership Map is owned by P7 rwb-decision, and the registry tables are P7. The section states where each story lands, which the two sources describe differently.
evidence: split_plan.json legacy: RWB-E1-072 primary PLT, slices RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-PLT-E1072-APP; RWB-E1-073 primary P3, slices RWB-P3-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1073-APP, RWB-P7-E1073-APP, RWB-P6-E1073-APP, RWB-P2-E1073-APP, RWB-P3-E1073-INF, RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG. Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: every /admin/rule-package path owner P7.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: The story set stays as the split plan gives it and the document states the capability owner: the registry and its endpoints are P7 rwb-decision, the embedded kit is PLT.

title: The effective-date job is a Quartz job owned by RW-COE in version 3 and a Temporal Schedule in rwb-decision in Architecture v5
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 names RulePackageEffectiveDateJob, a Quartz job at 00:01 owned by RW-COE. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-20 rule promote at 00:01 to rwb-decision as a Temporal Schedule and retires the shared Quartz tables. The job name, the mechanism and the owner all move.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 4: 'The effective-date job is RulePackageEffectiveDateJob, a Quartz job at 00:01 owned by RW-COE'. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: 'JOB-20 | Rule promote | 00:01 | rwb-decision | Schedule -> RulePackageInForce'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: Keep the name RulePackageEffectiveDateJob as the step and state that it runs as JOB-20, a Temporal Schedule in rwb-decision (P7), which publishes RulePackageInForce (EV-30).

title: Decision-record write path and activity order change with ADR-022
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: 1 The design on one page; 7 Use from Temporal; 8 Data
description: Version 3 writes one decision_log_entry through WriteDecisionLogActivity and only then applies the state through ApplyStateActivity. The Temporal and Drools design merges the two into one RecordAndApply activity because Architecture v5 (ADR-022) writes the decision record, the state change and the outbox row in one transaction, then collects the record into the central ledger in rwb-decision. The source document of this work package is the loser of that conflict.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 7: 'The workflow calls WriteDecisionLogActivity ... Only after that write does the workflow call ApplyStateActivity'. Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14: 'the separate WriteDecisionLog and ApplyState activities become one RecordAndApply activity'; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: Section 7 states the single RecordAndApply step and keeps the version 3 order as the superseded statement, with ADR-022 as the decision.

title: The rule store is counted in one schema in version 3 and distributed over 19 schemas in the target
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 counts 93 tables in the single recovery schema, of which the rule store is two new tables and four added columns. Architecture v5 places every table in one of 19 service schemas with one login each, so the same 93 tables are distributed and the count is no longer one schema's count. The document keeps the count and has to say what it counts.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 8: 'Physical Schema v6 counts 93 tables: the previous 92, plus rule_package and rule_package_version, less payment_match_rule'. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29: '19 RECOVERY SCHEMAS - ONE LOGIN EACH'; Template and Rules R6: the split into rwb_* schemas is new work (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB stories).
owner_role: ACE team (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: Keep 93 as the count of the target table set and state that the registry's four tables are in schema rwb_decision; the distribution is the RWB-PLT-NF06-DB split work.

title: The UNIVERSAL package has no single owning service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Rules Engine Design v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 states that each package has one owner role and, by the realignment, one owning service. The UNIVERSAL package (R-UNI-01 to 50) applies in every service, and neither source names one service that evaluates it for the others.
evidence: Rules Engine Design v3 section 2: 'Each package has one owner role, RW-COE, and one hit policy, FIRST_MATCH'. Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13: 'UNIVERSAL rules (R-UNI) apply in every service'.
owner_role: TechX (suggested; any team may pick up this story)
proposed: UNIVERSAL is evaluated in every service from its own copy of the same approved version, with authoring, scenarios and approval in rwb-decision (P7).
